papers.title: Computational Fluid Simulation of Fibrinogen around Dental Implant Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet treatment of titanium implants makes their surfaces hydrophilic and enhances osseointegration. However, the mechanism is not fully understood. This study hypothesizes that the recruitment of fibrinogen, a critical molecule for blood clot formation and wound healing, is influenced by the degrees of hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity of the implant surfaces. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) implant models were created for fluid flow simulation. The hydrophilicity level was expressed by the contact angle between the implant surface and blood plasma, ranging from 5° (superhydrophilic), 30° (hydrophilic) to 50° and 70° (hydrophobic), and 100° (hydrorepellent). The mass of fibrinogen flowing into the implant interfacial zone (fibrinogen infiltration) increased in a time dependent manner, with a steeper slope for surfaces with greater hydrophilicity. The mass of blood plasma absorbed into the interfacial zone (blood plasma infiltration) was also promoted by the hydrophilic surfaces but it was rapid and non-time-dependent. There was no linear correlation between the fibrinogen infiltration rate and the blood plasma infiltration rate. These results suggest that hydrophilic implant surfaces promote both fibrinogen and blood plasma infiltration to their interface. However, the infiltration of the two components were not proportional, implying a selectively enhanced recruitment of fibrinogen by hydrophilic implant surfaces.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing, porous structure design, stress shielding, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), or surface roughness characterization relevant to AM biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究亲疏水性对纤维蛋白原在种植体界面富集的影响
summary_zh.method: 构建不同接触角(5°-100°)的CFD模型进行流体模拟
summary_zh.result: 亲水表面促进纤维蛋白原浸润，但与血浆浸润不成比例
summary_zh.validation: 纯数值模拟，无实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how implant surface hydrophilicity influences fibrinogen recruitment, which is critical for osseointegration.
summary_en.method: Computational fluid dynamics models of dental implants with varying contact angles (5° to 100°) were used to simulate fibrinogen and blood plasma infiltration.
summary_en.result: Hydrophilic surfaces enhanced fibrinogen infiltration in a time-dependent manner, but the infiltration rates of fibrinogen and blood plasma were not linearly correlated.
summary_en.validation: The study is purely computational with no experimental validation.

papers.title: Degradation and Biocompatibility of AZ31 Magnesium Alloy Implants In Vitro and In Vivo: A Micro-Computed Tomography Study in Rats.
papers.abstract: In current orthodontic practice, miniscrew implants (MSIs) for anchorage and bone fixation plates (BFPs) for surgical orthodontic treatment are commonly used. MSIs and BFPs that are made of bioabsorbable material would avoid the need for removal surgery. We investigated the mechanical, degradation and osseointegration properties and the bone-implant interface strength of the AZ31 bioabsorbable magnesium alloy to assess its suitability for MSIs and BFPs. The mechanical properties of a Ti alloy (TiA), AZ31 Mg alloy (MgA), pure Mg and poly-L-lactic acid (PLA) were investigated using a nanoindentation test. Also, pH changes in the solution and degradation rates were determined using immersion tests. Three-dimensional, high-resolution, micro-computed tomography (CT) of implants in the rat femur was performed. Biomechanical push-out testing was conducted to calculate the maximum shear strength of the bone-implant interface. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), histological analysis and an evaluation of systemic inflammation were performed. MgA has mechanical properties similar to those of bone, and is suitable for implants. The degradation rate of MgA was significantly lower than that of Mg. MgA achieved a significantly higher bone-implant bond strength than TiA. Micro-CT revealed no significant differences in bone density or bone-implant contact between TiA and MgA. In conclusion, the AZ31 Mg alloy is suitable for both MSIs and BFPs.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究AZ31镁合金用于微型螺钉和骨固定板，与髋关节植入物和股骨柄的生物力学量化无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on biodegradable magnesium alloy for orthodontic miniscrew implants and bone fixation plates in rats, with no quantification of hip implant stress shielding, micromotion, or femoral stem biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估AZ31镁合金用于口腔植入物的降解和生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 通过纳米压痕、浸泡试验、micro-CT和推出测试表征。
summary_zh.result: AZ31镁合金力学性能接近骨骼，降解率低于纯镁，骨-植入物结合强度高于钛合金。
summary_zh.validation: 大鼠股骨体内植入后micro-CT和组织学分析。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the suitability of AZ31 magnesium alloy for bioabsorbable miniscrew implants and bone fixation plates in orthodontics.
summary_en.method: Mechanical properties were assessed via nanoindentation, degradation via immersion tests, and osseointegration via micro-CT and push-out tests in rat femurs.
summary_en.result: AZ31 alloy exhibited bone-like mechanical properties, lower degradation rate than pure Mg, and higher bone-implant bond strength than Ti alloy.
summary_en.validation: In vivo implantation in rat femur with micro-CT, histological, and biomechanical testing.
